page: Microsoft Azure D2ls_v5 is an entry-tier compute instance within the general-purpose D-series family, configured with a low memory-to-vCPU profile. The instance provides 2 vCPUs allocated across 1 physical core with 2 threads per core using hyperthreading. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for AVX, AVX-512, and cryptographic instruction sets like AES and SHA-NI.

System memory consists of 4.0 GB of RAM, yielding 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server does not bundle local disk storage or physical GPUs, requiring reliance on remote Azure storage disks for operating system and data requirements. Without bundled local NVMe storage, disk throughput is bound by network-attached storage limits and hypervisor configurations.

Benchmark results demonstrate moderate single-threaded capability alongside constrained multi-core throughput. Single-core evaluations reveal mid-range performance, with stress-ng recording 1889.98 and Geekbench achieving 1589.0. However, multi-threaded metrics place in the lowest quartile due to the two-vCPU hardware ceiling, yielding 1932.38 in stress-ng multi-core and 1861.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Memory bandwidth is bounded, registering 14.32 GB/sec for uncached 256MB reads and 13.3 GB/sec for writes. Redis key-value workloads reach 1.98 million SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 3.55 GB/sec.

Given its lean resource footprint and lack of integrated storage, the D2ls_v5 offers a cost-conscious entry point for applications requiring dedicated Intel vCPUs without extensive memory overhead. Appropriate workloads include lightweight microservices, basic web servers, automated background jobs, CI/CD runners, and edge orchestration tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure D2ls_v5 is a lean general-purpose virtual machine designed for entry-level computational tasks requiring dedicated CPU resources. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, supplying 2 vCPUs from a single physical core via hyperthreading. The configuration includes 4.0 GB of memory, translating to a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance provides no integrated local disk storage and no GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached persistent storage volumes. Benchmark data shows standard single-core compute performance, reaching 1589.0 in Geekbench single-core, though overall throughput is limited by the two-thread capacity. With memory read bandwidth of 14.32 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 13.3 GB/sec, the D2ls_v5 is best suited for small-scale applications, including lightweight web serving, microservice hosting, development environments, and auxiliary automated task runners.
